messages:
oliver (infra): Noticing a weird pattern in ap-southeast1: post-firmware rollout some nodes show long read-thaw windows causing attach stalls and janitor queues to pile up.
tina (sre): Yep. GPU pod start failures climbing; warm pool waits spike. Preemptible attach errs ~9% last 10m.
sam (storage): Telemetry: drives with sustained small random reads enter a recovery phase (we're calling it 'thaw') where latency slowly ramps for ~20-60s. Correlated with firmware v3.0.7.
drew (oncall): Node symptoms: ephemeral writes succeed but reads backblock, scratch cleanup times out. Older SSD firmware didn't show this.
deploy-bot: firmware-rollout/ap-southeast1 finished at 3510011200 by release-ci.
oliver (infra): Immediate ask: can we deprioritize janitor and background trims on affected racks to free read windows?
tina (sre): Doing `. set-janitor-cadence --region ap-southeast1 --factor 0.25` now. Also cordoning low-priority GPU pools.
sam (storage): Quick grep from nvme log: ```
[14:45:01] nvme1n1: read_thaw_start
[14:45:22] nvme1n1: read_thaw_end duration=21s retries=3
[14:45:22] nvme1n1: linux: bio submit delayed 2100ms
```
tina (sre): That lines up with attach tracer: `/k8s/attach` p99s hitting ~2s.
oliver (infra): Plan proposal: 1) throttle janitor/trims on affected racks 2) set scheduler zone-avoid for degraded racks 3) if thaw windows persist after 30m, rollback firmware on 3 canaries 4) if rollback fails, start rolling drains with live-migrate to other zones (cost impact flagged).
drew (oncall): Who runs rollback? storage owns it with infra support?
sam (storage): I'll take rollback on canaries. Command staged: `fw-ctl roll-to --device /dev/nvme1 --from 3.0.7 --to 3.0.6 --confirm --meta "read-thaw"` on 3 nodes first.
marco (product): Heads up: Dedicated customers in ap-southeast1 may see slower GPU starts. We should prepare a short console banner if customer-visible latency continues >30m.
tina (sre): Also enabling a temporary routing rule: `route.batch.low -> us-east1` for tolerant jobs to relieve ap-southeast1.
oliver (infra): Status after janitor throttle: read p95 improved from 420ms -> 160ms. But intermittent 1-2s outliers remain.
drew (oncall): Any SMART signals?
sam (storage): SMART NVM logs show rising 'media_errors' on a subset but below critical thresholds. Vendor says it's likely firmware interaction with hot small-read patterns causing internal GC-like micro-recovery. They provided hotpatch but recommended rollback.
deploy-bot: Hotpatch available at 3510012300 as build hotfix-3.0.7a.
tina (sre): I prefer rollback over untested hotpatch for now. Sam, roll canaries?
sam (storage): Rolling rollback to 3 canaries at 3510012400 now. Will stream logs.
oliver (infra): Finance note: cross-region fallback for Dedicated will add ~+$12k/day while rebalancing. Flagging finance lead.
marco (product): OK, prepare incident note draft in case we need to publicize. Keep wording minimal: "Investigating storage firmware issue affecting instance startup times in AP-SOUTHEAST1."
drew (oncall): Created incident INC-2026-3510012345. Keep updates concise.
sam (storage): Canary rollback result: canary-a p95 attach -> 85ms, no thaw events in last 10m. Starting batched rollback (20 nodes/hr).
tina (sre): Good. Once batched rollback passes first 60 nodes we'll lift some scheduling avoids.
oliver (infra): TL;DR: firmware v3.0.7 causes read 'thaw' windows under hot small-read load, we throttled janitor to buy time, rolling rollback in progress, routing to other regions for non-critical batch.
drew (oncall): Update in 20. Post only critical logs unless asked.
